title: Microsoft Authenticator: iCloud backup and restore of account entries on iOS
summary: The briefing passes: its backup prerequisites, restored-account behaviour and passkey controls agree with Microsoft's documentation. It accurately reports the stale roadmap dates as targets and distinguishes the documented user experience from unconfirmed tenant controls and feature-specific licensing.

claims.quote: Users of the Microsoft Authenticator app on iOS will be able to back up account names

claims.claim: The planned backup covers Microsoft work or school account names.
claims.quote: including Microsoft work or school accounts

claims.claim: The planned backup covers Microsoft personal account names.
claims.quote: Microsoft personal accounts

claims.claim: The planned backup covers third-party accounts such as Amazon and Google.
claims.quote: third-party accounts like Amazon or Google

claims.claim: The roadmap specifies iCloud and iCloud Keychain as the backup services.
claims.quote: using iCloud and iCloud Keychain

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing, second paragraph
claims.claim: Microsoft documents iOS Authenticator backup through iCloud and recovery of account entries on a new phone.
claims.quote: Use the following steps to back up Microsoft Authenticator on your old phone, restore it on your new phone, and set up passkeys again when needed.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Backup is user-opt-in through the user's iCloud settings rather than a documented tenant enablement switch.
claims.quote: To back up Authenticator on an iOS device, enable iCloud Drive, Keychain, and Backup for Authenticator. ... Turn on the Authenticator toggle.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant-wide administrator UI or API switch specifically governing Authenticator iOS account backup and restore is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Authenticator iOS iCloud backup restore disable administrator tenant Intune app configuration Microsoft Graph backup setting'; read transfer, Intune restrictions and Graph Authenticator configuration/featureSettings beta references; no tenant backup switch.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope
claims.claim: The documented iOS backup procedure requires iCloud Drive to be enabled.
claims.quote: Enable iCloud Drive on your iOS device.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The documented iOS backup procedure requires iCloud Keychain to be enabled.
claims.quote: Enable iCloud Keychain on your iOS device.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The documented iOS backup procedure requires iCloud Backup to be enabled.
claims.quote: Enable iCloud Backup on your iOS device.

claims.claim: The user turns on Authenticator under Apple Account > iCloud > Saved to iCloud.
claims.quote: Go to Apple Account > iCloud > Saved to iCloud and search for Authenticator. ... Turn on the Authenticator toggle.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: For a work or school account, only its account name is restored.
claims.quote: Work or school accounts ... Only the account name is restored.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A restored work or school account requires opening the account and signing in again to complete setup.
claims.quote: To complete setup on the new phone, open the account and sign in again.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: A restored work account may show a red sign-in prompt.
claims.quote: You might see red text that says "Sign in to add your account."

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A personal Microsoft account using only a one-time password code has its verification code entry restored.
claims.quote: If the account uses only a one-time password code that refreshes every 30 seconds, the verification code entry is restored.

claims.claim: A personal Microsoft account also using passwordless sign-in has only its account name restored.
claims.quote: If the account also uses passwordless sign-in, only the account name is restored and you must sign in again to complete setup.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Third-party accounts using one-time password codes have their verification code entries restored.
claims.quote: Third-party accounts (Amazon, Facebook, Gmail, etc.) ... These accounts typically use a one-time password code that refreshes every 30 seconds. ... The verification code entry is restored.

claims.claim: The iCloud backup described by the roadmap includes the TOTP credentials behind the restored one-time-code entries.
claims.quote: using iCloud and iCloud Keychain. This enables secure, end-to-end encrypted backup of account names and TOTP credentials.

claims.claim: Learn instructs users whose accounts enforce passkeys to set up a passkey for the new phone before removing the old device.
claims.quote: If passkeys are enforced for the account, set up a passkey for the new phone before removing the old device.

claims.claim: A passkey saved in a synced credential manager might not need to be created again.
claims.quote: If the passkey was saved to a synced credential manager, such as Microsoft Password Manager, Google Password Manager, or Apple iCloud Keychain, you might not need to create a new passkey.

claims.claim: Learn tells users to verify that a synced passkey is available before removing the old device.
claims.quote: Verify the passkey is available before removing the old device.

claims.claim: Passkeys are handled separately from Authenticator account backup.
claims.quote: Passkeys are handled separately from Authenticator account backup.

claims.claim: A passkey saved only on the old phone requires a new passkey for the new phone.
claims.quote: If a passkey was saved only to the old phone, add a new passkey for the new phone.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises keeping the old phone until sign-in to needed accounts and resources works on the new phone.
claims.quote: Keep your old phone until you confirm that you can sign in to the accounts and resources you use most often from the new phone.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: For an unavailable restore option, Learn says to verify backup was enabled on the old phone.
claims.quote: Restore from backup isn't available. ... Verify backup was enabled on the old phone

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: For an unavailable restore option, Learn says to verify the same recovery account is used.
claims.quote: Verify backup was enabled on the old phone, you're using the same recovery account, and you're restoring to the same device type.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance: After rollout

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Licensing specific to Authenticator account backup and restore is not yet published, so the model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com Microsoft Authenticator backup restore license pricing'; read transfer page and Entra licensing authentication table. General MFA and passkey licensing do not state a licence for account backup/restore.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cited Learn transfer page specifies no licence, price or meter for backup and restore.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Authenticator backup restore iCloud licensing price meter free'; opened https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-transfer-authenticator-new-phone in full; it gives steps and behaviour, not licensing or charges.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No price or meter specific to Authenticator account backup and restore is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Authenticator backup restore iCloud licensing price meter free' and 'site:learn.microsoft.com Microsoft Authenticator backup restore license pricing'; read transfer page and Entra licensing excerpts; no feature-specific rate or meter.

claims.claim: No administrator role is documented for performing Authenticator account backup or restore itself.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Authenticator backup restore iOS version requirements administrator role tenant backup disable'; read transfer page in full and Graph Authenticator policy reference; no administrator role for the user backup/restore procedure.

claims.where: What's changing, last paragraph; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The supplied record and transfer page do not establish rollout mechanics or map the planned improvements to a confirmed launched status.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Authenticator iOS improved backup restore automatic default enabled rollout minimum version administrator role'; read record and transfer page. A separate Entra announcement concerns device-bound passkey restore, not launch confirmation for this account-backup item.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the transfer page states a minimum Authenticator version for this backup and restore procedure.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Authenticator backup restore iOS version requirements administrator role tenant backup disable'; read roadmap record and full transfer page; neither specifies an Authenticator version for account backup/restore.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the transfer page states an iOS version for this backup and restore procedure.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Authenticator backup restore iOS version requirements administrator role tenant backup disable'; read roadmap record and full transfer page; neither states an iOS version for account backup/restore.

claims.where: Why it matters, second paragraph; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that this account-backup change changes behaviour for users who do not enable backup or restore onto a new phone.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Authenticator iOS improved backup restore automatic default enabled rollout minimum version administrator role'; read record and transfer page. Neither describes a change for users outside backup/restore; the passkey-restore announcement addresses existing backup users.

claims.claim: After opting in to passkey profiles, the self-service control is at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Security > Authentication methods > Policies > Passkey (FIDO2) > Configure > Allow self-service set up.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Security > Authentication methods > Policies. ... Select Passkey (FIDO2). ... On the Configure tab, set Allow self-service set up to Yes.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations/fido2 updates the tenant passkey policy, including its self-service registration setting.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations/fido2 ... "isSelfServiceRegistrationAllowed": true

claims.claim: Authentication Policy Administrator is the least privileged role for the passkey policy control.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least an Authentication Policy Administrator.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Allow self-service set up governs users registering passkeys, not Authenticator account backup.
claims.quote: If set to No, users can't register a passkey by using Security info, even if passkeys (FIDO2) are enabled by the Authentication methods policy.

claims.claim: The passkey self-service setting is tenant-wide rather than a per-profile setting.
claims.quote: This setting is a global policy; it's not on the profile level.

claims.claim: The Graph request-body property controlling passkey self-service registration is isSelfServiceRegistrationAllowed.
claims.quote: isSelfServiceRegistrationAllowed | Boolean | Determines if users can register new passkeys (FIDO2).

claims.claim: The cited passkey page places its Configure-tab instructions after opting in to passkey profiles.
claims.quote: Select Passkey (FIDO2). Select the link in the banner text to opt-in to using passkeys profiles. ... On the Configure tab, set Allow self-service set up to Yes.

claims.claim: After opting in to passkey profiles, administrators cannot opt out.
claims.quote: After you opt in to enable passkey profiles, you can't opt out.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Intune's Block iCloud backup setting stops users backing up supervised iOS/iPadOS devices to iCloud.
claims.quote: Block iCloud backup: Yes stops users from backing up devices to iCloud.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Intune's Block iCloud Keychain sync setting disables syncing credentials stored in Keychain to iCloud.
claims.quote: Block iCloud Keychain sync: Yes disables syncing credentials stored in the Keychain to iCloud.

claims.claim: Starting with iOS/iPadOS 13.0, Block iCloud backup requires a supervised device.
claims.quote: Block iCloud backup ... Starting with iOS/iPadOS 13.0, this setting requires supervised devices.

claims.claim: Starting with iOS/iPadOS 13.0, Block iCloud Keychain sync requires a supervised device.
claims.quote: Block iCloud Keychain sync ... Starting with iOS/iPadOS 13.0, this setting requires supervised devices.

claims.claim: Learn tells users to contact their administrator or help desk if self-service passkey setup is not allowed.
claims.quote: If your IT admin doesn't allow self-service passkey setup, contact your admin or help desk for the approved recovery or registration process.
